## Positions the author explicitly frames against

- *Following one specific threat-modelling methodology in this document.* Methodologies can impose cognitive barriers on newcomers, and MAESTRO-like methodologies also cover non-agentic threats; the document uses its reference architecture instead, while recommending practitioners pick a methodology that suits them (p. 12).
- *Established methodologies applied unchanged.* STRIDE and PASTA are rooted in traditional cyber vulnerabilities and "must be expanded or mapped to AI vulnerabilities" [V] (p. 12).
- *The LLM Top 10 entries alone, for agentic threats.* Threat by threat, the Navigator says the related LLM Top 10 entry covers the agentic threat only partially or that agentic AI extends it (e.g. T6 against LLM01, T1 against LLM04, T2 and T3 against LLM06, T5 against LLM09, T11 against LLM01 and LLM05) (pp. 21–32).

## Citation and source-integrity notes

**Conversion.** The original is a 53-page PDF exported from Word on macOS (PDF title field "Microsoft Word - FINAL DRAFT__Agentic AI - Threats and Mitigations 1.1.docx"; created 2025-12-07 10:18 NZDT), at `sources/original/owasp-agentic-threats-mitigations.pdf`, sha256 `65e3bd59f99c411b055c6caf2bac96ab361dff8c010e4bef532a593ce10345ff`, fetched 2026-10-11. It has a born-digital text layer. The tape `sources/converted/owasp-agentic-threats-mitigations.md` (1,985 lines, 14,767 words) is that layer extracted with `pdftotext -layout` (poppler 26.08.0). Post-conversion check: 53 form feeds, one per page; footers run "Page 1" to "Page 52"; the last page (Project Supporters) is present; no truncation marker.

**Title, version and date.** The cover gives the title "Agentic AI - Threats and Mitigations", "Version 1.1" and "December 2025"; the PDF title field adds "FINAL DRAFT" and the version "1.1". The resource page's first-publication date (2025-02-17, from the fetch metadata) is not in the tape, which names no earlier version.

**Page anchors.** The cover has no footer, so printed page N is PDF page N+1. Page N's text ends at its footer line in the tape; p. 1 ends at line 40, p. 10 at 293, p. 16 at 527, p. 20 at 709, p. 32 at 1227, p. 33 (footer only) at 1228, p. 42 at 1609, p. 49 at 1872, p. 52 at 1985.

**Table of Content against the footers.** The printed Table of Content (p. 2) gives Agentic Threats Taxonomy Navigator 20, Mitigation Strategies 31, Example Threat Models 39, Acknowledgements 45, Sponsors 46, Project Supporters 47; the footers put these at pp. 21, 34, 43, 50, 51, 52. Citations here follow the footers.

**Internal mismatches recorded as printed.** The Introduction promises threat models for "four example scenarios" (p. 3); three follow (pp. 43–49). Mitigation Strategies opens with "five playbooks" (p. 34); six follow. The supply-chain box (p. 14) says no new supply-chain threat was introduced, while the table and Navigator carry T17 (pp. 19, 28–29). Playbook 6 cites "Step 5: Multi-Agent System Threats" (p. 41), where the Navigator's multi-agent question is Step 6 (p. 31); Playbooks 4 and 5 cite step names ("Authentication & Identity Security", "Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) Threats") that differ from the Navigator's headings. The mapping table puts Insecure Inter-Agent Protocol Abuse under Playbooks 3 and 4 (p. 34); neither playbook's "Mitigates" line names it (pp. 37, 39). Playbook 5's name differs between the mapping table and its heading (pp. 34, 40). Threat names vary: T17 "Supply Chain Compromise" (table) and "Supply Chain Attacks" (Navigator); T9 "Identity Spoofing & Impersonation / Agent Identity Compromise" (table) and "Identity Spoofing and Impersonation" (Navigator). Playbook 2's last detective bullet is printed twice (p. 37), and Playbook 5's reactive and detective steps repeat Playbook 1's bullets (pp. 35, 40–41).

**Licence page.** The licence is CC BY-SA 4.0 (p. 1), so scope is `open`. The page's Attribution Guidelines name the asset as "OWASP Top 10 for LLMs - GenAI Red Teaming Guide" [V], a different OWASP document from this one (p. 1).

**Disclaimer.** The document states that its information is for general informational purposes only and does not constitute legal advice. Links to third-party websites are provided only for convenience; OWASP does not recommend or endorse their contents (p. 1) [AP].

**Source and text-layer defects.** On p. 14 the RAG sentence is malformed in both the rendered original and the text layer: it reads "a core mechanism in modern agentic AI systems, awareness and response accuracy". It is paraphrased here, not quoted. On p. 4 the Russell and Norvig quotation's quote marks are unbalanced in the text layer; only its inner clause is quoted here. On p. 50 the text layer includes "Hariprasad Holla, CrowdStrike" in the continued contributor list, which the rendered page does not show; the rendered page shows 38 contributors. Spellings kept as printed: "Trend Mico" (p. 50), "LLM05:2025 - Insecure Output Handling" (p. 27), "scepticism" (p. 30) beside "skepticism" (p. 19).

**Table layout.** The Detailed Threat Model (pp. 16–19), the patterns table (pp. 10–11), the mapping table (pp. 34–35) and the Acknowledgements (p. 50) are multi-column; in the tape the columns interleave line by line, and in T5 and T7 the description and mitigation cells are offset. Their cells are paraphrased here, not quoted, except for short runs inside one tape line.

**Figures.** Figure content (pp. 6, 8, 10, 16) is described from renders and marked [AP]; the threat-ID placements on p. 16 were read from a 220-dpi crop. Image scope is otherwise text-only (see Coverage).
